newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-TRANSPORT FIRM ADVISOR TENDER GETS 40 BIDS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-TRANSPORT FIRM ADVISOR TENDER GETS 40 BIDS.

text.p: Lithuania's European Affairs ministry said on Friday that 21 companies submitted applications to advise the government on the privatisation of the Lithuanian Sea Shipping company (LISCO).
It also said in a statement that 19 firms said they wanted to advise the government on the privatisation of the country's biggest stevedoring firm KLASCO.
Nomura International, KPMG London, Union Bank of Switzerland, Barents Group, D. Carnegie, Tufton Oceanic were mentioned among the contenders.
The ministry said in a statement that the tender commission will decide on the short list of companies to bid to be lead advisors in the two privatisations next week.
KLASCO is the biggest stevedoring company in Klaipeda port, handling over seven million cargoes per year. The ferry terminal is an integral part of the firm.

LISCO is 80 percent state-controlled. Its share capital stands at around 471 million litas. The company owns 38 vessels and together with German partners operates two vessels on the carrying ro-ro cargos.
